name: eevee-performance-profiler-attribution
purpose: Verify Eevee profiler attribution, final-render source identity, safe GLSL Function material feature snapshots, the viewport shared Draw Sync/Draw Submission timing ledger, event-loop publication without active redraw polling across EEVEE Instance recreation, and the structured Outliner performance view.
passCriteria: The generated Eevee scenes must render with the profiler enabled. Render reports must declare CPU wall-time timing, inclusive scope accounting, the final-render initialization exclusion, and non-empty View Layer and Render View source fields, and must contain shadow light/context attribution, probe work, Filter.BeforeComposite activity, and ReadResult timing. Measured Shader Waits must have non-negative CPU/frame-share values whenever present, and Material Sync must have positive Total requests whenever present. The Filter report must include Material Sync and Pass Readback with positive Total passes/data, non-negative CPU/readback-share values, and typed pass counts that reconcile to the aggregate. The viewport report must declare shared draw-cycle coverage, expose a finite non-negative Profiler Accounting CPU outside Draw CPU, reconcile Draw CPU with one non-zero Sync root plus one non-zero Submission root, run each direct phase once, expose EEVEE Begin/End Sync module groups, keep child totals within their parent roots, and report dependency-graph evaluation separately with an evaluation-serial label. It must publish completed 1/1 sampling plus a newer capture sequence after a known scene update without active redraw polling. After that baseline is stable, a live material update must add one GLSL Function material without accessing invalid GPU material source data, and publication must resume with `GLSL Mats=1` after a Solid-to-Rendered transition recreates the EEVEE Instance. A replacement source may use a new Source ID and restart its capture sequence. A live Outliner in EEVEE_PERFORMANCE mode must redraw while structured snapshots are published. Reports must omit duplicate or speculative sections: Top CPU Stages, Sync Texture Loads, Sync Objects, Film Outputs, Filter Costs, Render Texture Costs, and Hints.
